title: 3Sum
prompt: Given an integer array `nums`, return all the unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j`, `i != k`, `j != k`, and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The result must not contain duplicate triplets. You may return the triplets in any order, but each triplet's elements should be sorted in ascending order.

examples.explanation: The two distinct triplets that sum to 0 are (-1,-1,2) and (-1,0,1).

hints: Sorting the array first makes duplicate-skipping and two-pointer scanning much easier.
Fix one number, then the problem reduces to finding two other numbers (in the remaining sorted array) that sum to its negation — a two-pointer sweep.
After sorting, skip over duplicate values for the fixed index (and for the two pointers once a match is found) to avoid emitting the same triplet twice.

solution.approach: Sort the array first. Then for each index i (skipping duplicate values to avoid repeat triplets), use two pointers, lo starting right after i and hi starting at the end, to find pairs that sum to -nums[i]. If the sum is too small, move lo right; if too large, move hi left; if it matches, record the triplet and advance both pointers past any duplicate values. This avoids the O(n^3) brute force by turning the inner search into an O(n) two-pointer scan for each of the n outer choices.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra space, excluding output and sort space
